text:
maria-support: heads-up — Acme support ticket: their integration started returning the wrong tool result after the 14:02 deploy. They call "billing.calculate" but the payload looks like it came from billing.estimate. Repro below, customer says it started at ~14:08 UTC.

maria-support: repro (redacted):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
 -d '{"tool":"billing.calculate","args":{"customer_id":"acct_9876"}}'
```

maria-support: response body (customer received):
```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "tool": "billing.estimate",
  "result": {"estimate_total": 42.17} 
}
```

maria-support: their integration is schema validating the response and failing. customer is blocked in production, escalating to P2.

tim-support: ack. can you paste the request_id / client logs and the exact time they saw it? also, do they have a tool UUID stored anywhere?

maria-support: request_id: rq_2026_03_17_14_09_03, they call via our hosted SDK (v2.1.4). they do not pin UUIDs, only alias name.

deploy-bot: services/registry deploy completed at 2026-03-17T14:02:18Z by ci/cd-pipeline #4827.

nate-eng: looking. I see the registry backfill job (alias-migration) ran at 14:01 and wrote a bunch of alias -> handle mappings. quickly checking logs for billing.calculate...

nate-eng: found it: backfill created alias key `billing.calculate` pointing at handle uuid hdl_8a3f (which is billing.estimate). previous canonical mapping was hdl_b1c2 (billing.calculate old). it looks like the backfill used casefolded names when deduping; there was a conflict with a historical alias `Billing.Calculate` that got normalized and picked the wrong target. :eyes:

linda-registry: yeah that matches what I see in the audit. the migration script did case-insensitive dedupe and then preferred the newer handle when collisions occurred. we missed preserving exact-casing canonical ownership.

kevin-product: is this a client-side cache TTL problem or registry authoritative mapping change? customer says they restarted and still get the wrong tool.

nate-eng: authoritative mapping changed — the registry now resolves `billing.calculate` -> hdl_8a3f. SDK uses registry lookup + local TTL cache (30s). restart won't help if mapping is changed.

maria-support: customer wants immediate workaround. any quick mitigation?

linda-registry: two immediate options: 1) write a temporary alias mapping `billing.calculate` -> hdl_b1c2 (the original) in the registry to restore behavior; or 2) ask client to call by stable UUID (if they can update) or use the explicit new alias `billing.calculate_v2` if they accept new API semantics.

nate-eng: we should avoid manual alias write without root cause fixed — but for customer unblock we can create a targeted alias override for acct_9876 (namespaced aliases) so it only affects them. that's lower blast radius.
sre-oncall: will we need to purge edge caches after alias change? yes — we have alias->handle caches in edge CDN and SDK local TTL. plan: create namespaced alias for the customer, then purge edge and advise client to restart SDK.

maria-support: please do that asap. can we also get a statement I can send to the customer about cause and ETA?

linda-registry: action plan: (1) create namespaced alias `acct_9876:billing.calculate` -> hdl_b1c2 (10m) (2) purge edge alias cache key prefix `alias:billing.calculate` (5m) (3) add hotfix to migration script to prefer exact-case canonical owner and re-run reconciliation (30-60m).

nate-eng: I'll open a PR for the migration hotfix and run a dry reconciliation on staging first. I'll also run a targeted registry patch to restore the original mapping for acct_9876 now.

sre-oncall: running cache purge: POST /internal/cache/purge?prefix=alias%3Abilling.calculate -> response 202 accepted.

linda-registry: applied namespaced override for acct_9876, mapping now points at hdl_b1c2. monitoring audit for new writes.

maria-support: sent customer a message: "We've applied a temporary mapping for your account and purged caches. You should see correct responses after restarting your integration or waiting up to 30s. We're working on a permanent fix and will update you within 60 minutes."

kevin-product: follow-up Q — do we need to notify other customers who may be affected? any other aliases collided in the same run?

linda-registry: running a quick scan for collisions. preliminary: ~7 other aliases had conflicts but resolved to intended owner because canonical case matched new target. billing.calculate was an edge case because of a legacy alias that only differs by case.

nate-eng: I'll add a monitoring alert for alias-resolution churn during the next 24h and a script to report accounts that see handle changes for a given alias.

sre-oncall: prod checks look stable now for acct_9876 — calls return the expected schema after the override. leaving an incident marker for follow-up.

maria-support: thanks all — I'll keep the ticket updated. please post final remediation steps here when done so I can close the customer loop. :thumbsup:
